data_quality_notes:
Research phase completed and logged a RESEARCH COMPLETE block, so nothing here is truncated. 11 candidates captured, 11 published, 0 dropped on the reward-to-risk floor — every ratio below was recomputed by synthesis from the final entry, target and downside rather than carried over from the notes.

WHAT IS ACTIONABLE TODAY, AND IT IS NOT MUCH. This is a Saturday report. Of eleven ideas, exactly two can be acted on before Monday: the /MBTU6 cover at the Sunday 18:00 ET CME reopen, and the ETH limit at 2,100 in a 24/7 market. Seven of the remaining nine are limit orders sitting 2.7% to 14.1% below Friday's close that may never fill. The research phase checked all 18 Robinhood-listed coins and found a uniform, beta-ordered drift lower with no dislocation in any pair — config/strategy.md asks a weekend run to lean on crypto for actionable ideas and today crypto did not produce one. That is a real gap in this report, not a stylistic choice.

THE REWARD-TO-RISK CLUSTERING, FLAGGED AGAINST ITSELF. All six new long-term ideas compute between 2.53 and 2.68 against a 2.5 floor (ELV 2.53, LULU 2.54, ETH 2.55, CAG 2.56, KMPR 2.56, MDT 2.60, CME 2.68). That is the exact fingerprint of targets fitted to clear a bar, and the reader should treat it with suspicion. The research phase pre-emptively audited itself on this and the audit holds up on inspection: for every one of them the target was set first from something external and citable (company EPS guidance, a published sell-side target, a historical multiple, a stated ETH/BTC ratio), the bear case was set second from an observed price at or below the actual 150-day low, and the ENTRY was then solved for. The tell that distinguishes this from the failure mode is that every single long-term entry sits BELOW Friday's market — CME -2.7%, MDT -3.5%, LULU -5.6%, ELV -6.7%, CAG -9.3%, ETH -14.1% — and all seven are marked WAIT. Targets were never moved to rescue a ratio; if they had been, the entries would sit at or above the market. Three of the solved entries independently landed within a dollar of where insiders actually bought (ELV 368.6 vs purchases at 366.05-368.25; CAG 14.66 vs the CEO at 14.59; KMPR 27.00 vs five buyers at 26.34-26.53), which is a genuine cross-check rather than an after-the-fact dressing. The honest cost of the method, stated plainly: there is no margin of safety above the floor, so if the market comes to exactly these limits and no further, each position opens at the least attractive price the strategy permits. Treat every long-term entry below as a CEILING and prefer to be filled beneath it.

TWO STOPS WERE BREACHED AND IGNORED, AND THAT IS THE TOP OF THIS REPORT. Ranks 1 and 2 are not ideas, they are corrections. The /MBTU6 short is 21.7% offside past a 66,600 stop breached around 2026-08-20, and this is the THIRD consecutive report to request the cover — 2026-08-25 and 2026-08-26 both ranked it first and it is still open. TJX is 10.4% down past a 145.50 stop, a defined 3.5% risk carried to three times that. Neither carries a reward-to-risk because a loss realisation has none, and writing one would be fiction.

PORTFOLIO RISK THAT NO SINGLE IDEA BELOW SHOWS: the existing open book is one undiversified bet on Iran. XLE x3, DINO, DHT x2 and indirectly CCJ — six-plus of twenty open positions — all resolve on whether the Strait of Hormuz reopens, against this report's own stated cap of three ideas per driver. Nothing was added to that complex today and FRO, INSW, STNG, PBF, CVI, DK, VLO and MPC were all rejected partly on those grounds. Among today's NEW risk the cap holds: three ideas touch the rate path (CME, KMPR, the Fed contract) and they are not the same bet — CME monetises hedging volume in either direction, KMPR reinvests insurance float at higher-for-longer yields, and the Fed contract is a directional bet on September timing specifically.

REGIME CHANGE, FRIDAY. Every level in the existing open book was set before Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole debut flipped the market from pricing cuts to pricing hikes. The EEM cancellation at rank 3 is that repricing firing a kill switch the 2026-08-22 report wrote for itself.

SOURCES THAT FAILED, AND WHAT EACH COST. Yahoo Finance returned HTTP 429 for the entire session on every symbol, so there is NO VIX index level, NO DXY, no index futures (ES/NQ), no gold or WTI futures and no ^GSPC/^NDX/^DJI/^RUT in this report; ETF proxies (SPY/QQQ/IWM/GLD/VIXY) were substituted and are labelled as such everywhere they appear. This directly weakened the EEM cancellation, whose stated invalidation had a DXY leg that could not be measured — the hawkish leg is confirmed, the dollar leg is assumed, and that is disclosed in the idea's own key_risk. The /MBT futures quote could not be fetched either, so rank 1 uses CoinGecko BTC spot (77,836 live) as an explicitly labelled proxy; /MBT tracks spot within roughly 1%. Also failed: bls.gov (403 to WebFetch — release dates confirmed via search against bls.gov/schedule instead), Kalshi's /markets price fields (null; only /trades and /orderbook returned prices), Alpha Vantage (no API key), Stooq (404 on indices), and Finnhub for CFD indices (subscription required). Two tooling bugs worth fixing: `market_data.py events` keyword-matched a search for 'Fed' to a baseball market on pitcher Erick Fedde and is effectively broken for event contracts, and finnhub's insider feed for STNG is corrupt ($18.93B sell value, a buy at $5.87 on a $78 stock) and was discarded.

PRICES. All equity and ETF prices are the Friday 2026-08-28 16:00 ET close, verified as session=closed at synthesis time. On a Saturday that is the freshest honest equity price, not stale data. Crypto was re-quoted live at 11:42 ET (BTC 77,836, ETH 2,442.64). CAG's total debt could not be fetched and is named inside that idea's key_risk rather than quietly omitted — for a packaged-food turnaround, leverage is the usual failure mode, so it is the largest single unknown in the report.

HORIZON SKEW IS PRONOUNCED AND WAS NOT MANUFACTURED: 7 long_term, 3 swing, 1 intraday — and the intraday item is a futures cover, not a trade. There are zero intraday setups because it is Saturday and the US cash sessions are shut, so there was no intraday setup to have. Per config/strategy.md this is stated rather than apologised for, and nothing was padded to balance the mix.

COVERAGE NOT REACHED, for the next run: systematic small/micro-cap screening beyond the seven names hand-screened in the addendum, ADRs and international, the September S&P index rebalance, and the FDA calendar beyond PRAX and SVRA. Only ONE event contract is published against a config that actively wants them — Robinhood lists 77 economics, 62 crypto and 5 metals markets, but only the Fed decision markets could be confirmed against a Robinhood URL, and guessing at venue availability would break a non-negotiable. The December Fed contract was rejected on an 8-cent bid-ask spread that eats the entire edge.

REJECTED WITH REASONS LOGGED: CIEN, AVGO, FN, PRAX, SVRA, FRO, INSW, STNG, PBF/CVI/DK/VLO/MPC, a short /M2KU6, KXFEDDECISION-26DEC, a 2s10s flattener (could not verify Robinhood carries /ZT), and FSBC — whose seven insider 'buys' were all at exactly $44.00 on exactly 2026-07-22, which is a capital raise at a fixed offering price, not six people independently deciding a stock is cheap. A dollar total is not a cluster; a distribution of dates and prices is.

=== RED TEAM (phase 2c) ===
Cut one idea, downgraded three, fixed two sources and one mislabelled direction. Ten remain.

CUT: the Kalshi September no-hike contract (was rank 11). Its own key_risk and counter_argument establish that fed funds futures price a September hike 9-12 points more hawkish than this contract, and the counter_argument names the error precisely — 'treating that gap as my edge rather than as my error is the exact reasoning that keeps losing trades open' — then takes the position anyway. That is the falsification step written down and ignored. On the report's own fair value the edge is 1-6 cents on a binary; on futures-implied fair value it is 10-13 cents negative. Verified against the live Kalshi book before cutting (H0 53/54c, H25 46/47c): the prices and the polarity in the report were correct, so this is a judgement kill and not a data error. The validator's 404 on the Kalshi endpoint was transient — that URL returns 200.

THE MAIN FINDING — the bear cases, not the targets, are where the arithmetic was flattered. The research phase self-audited its reward-to-risk cluster (2.53-2.68 against a 2.5 floor), argued the free variable was the ENTRY rather than the target, and invited an independent check. The audit is correct about the numerator and wrong about the denominator. It claims bear cases were 'set from an observed price, usually at or below the actual 150-day low'. Recomputed from fetched OHLCV, that holds for three names and fails for three:
  CONSERVATIVE — LULU bear 88 vs 150d low 104.44 (-15.7%), CAG 11.00 vs 12.53 (-12.2%), KMPR 21.00 vs 22.69 (-7.4%). ETH 1,550 is the actual June low, cross-checked two ways.
  FLATTERED — CME bear 240 vs low 218.31 (+9.9%), ELV 300 vs 274.84 (+9.2%), MDT 78 vs 73.31 (+6.4%). Substituting the observed low collapses the published ratios to CME 1.71, MDT 1.77, ELV 1.85 — all below the 2.5 floor they were built to clear.
  The asymmetry is what matters: the three flattered ideas were the three largest positions in the book (4% each) and the three honest ones the smallest (2-2.5%). Sizing ran exactly inverse to robustness. A reader told 'ELV 2.53' and 'LULU 2.54' would take them for equivalent setups; they are not, because LULU's denominator absorbs a 15.7% break of its low while ELV's assumes the stock never revisits a price it traded at in March. Raising a bear case has the same arithmetic effect as lowering a target, and the self-audit only checked the target.
  Acted on by cutting conviction and size rather than by moving levels: CME 4->3 and 4%->3%, MDT 4->3 and 4%->3%, ELV 4->3 and 4%->2%. Bear cases were deliberately NOT rewritten to the observed lows — that would have tripped the enforce pass and auto-demoted all three on a standard this red team does not actually endorse (a 150-day low is one print, often a panic wick, not a considered downside). CME and MDT survive because their published two-rung plans average to almost exactly the price that clears 2.5 against the observed low (266 vs 264.51; 85 vs 84.94) — so both are conditional on BOTH rungs filling, and a first-rung-only fill is not the advertised trade. ELV fails even that test (356 average vs 350.60 required) and was cut hardest; it also rests on 2026 being the Medicaid margin trough while its own key_risk concedes the MLR is still rising and that every managed care insurer has called a false trough for two years. Re-ranked from 6 to 9 on that basis.

WHAT THE READER MUST NOT MISS: this report recommends buying nothing today. All seven long-term ideas are 'WAIT' limits below Friday's close (-2.7% to -14.0%), the top three ranks are two position exits and an order cancellation, and the only same-day new-money position in the book was the Kalshi contract, which is now cut. That is an honest outcome after a regime change and is not a criticism — but the report presents as ten ideas and is operationally 'close two losers, cancel one order, and leave seven resting limits'. Several of those limits will never fill; CAG at -9.3% and ETH at -14.0% require a real drawdown to trigger.

CORRELATION, and a risk nobody named: three of the surviving long-term ideas (ELV, KMPR, CAG) come from a single insider-cluster screen over beaten-down value, and all three run the same 'management called the trough and bought their own stock' mechanism. Separately, MDT (3.16%), CAG (4.35%) and KMPR (4.58%) are dividend-yield defensives being recommended in a report whose own market_context declares a hawkish repricing toward a hiking path. Bond proxies de-rating on rising rates is the classic loser in exactly the regime this report just called, and it appears in none of the three key_risk fields. Flagged rather than cut — the ideas are value cases, not yield cases — but the tension is real and unaddressed. One correlation the research phase flagged itself (ETH and the Fed no-hike contract sharing a driver) is resolved by the cut above.

LEFT STANDING WITH A CAVEAT: ETH's bear case is the most honest in the report, but its 3,500 target rests on an ETH/BTC ratio of 0.045 that is never anchored to anything — the notes justify it as 'the ratio normalising IS the flow thesis, so the target and the mechanism are the same claim', which is circular. No historical range for the ratio was cited. The entry sits 14% below market so this is largely academic, and conviction 3 / 2% already reflects it.

NOT CUT, AND DELIBERATELY SO: the three position actions at ranks 1-3. Covering the /MBTU6 short (-21.7% on a breached stop, leveraged and marked daily) and selling TJX (-10.4% on a breached stop) are the correct calls and the ranking is right — they are the only actions with money at stake today.

Kevin Warsh used his first Jackson Hole speech as Fed Chair on 2026-08-28 to say he is impressed with economic strength, that underlying inflation trends have NOT improved, and that the Fed has more work to do — while explicitly refusing to give forward guidance or publish a reaction function at all, as a stated governance philosophy. Odds of a September hike went from roughly 1-in-3 pre-speech to a majority expecting one; the Kalshi strip now prices September 47%, October 28%, December ~45%. Friday's tape is consistent with a hawkish repricing rather than a growth scare: GLD -3.24% (the single biggest move on the tape, a no-yield asset repricing), IWM -1.35% (small caps are the most rate-sensitive cohort), QQQ -0.65%, SPY -0.23%, VIXY +1.79%. The tell nobody should miss is that TLT fell only 0.30%. A hawkish shock that moves gold 3.2% and barely registers on the 20y+ long bond is the long end saying it finds the inflation-fighting credible — that is a flattener, not a bond bear market, and 10y-2y is already only +39bp. Two prints stand between here and the Sep 16 FOMC: August payrolls Fri Sep 4, and August CPI Fri Sep 11, three sessions before the meeting. catalyst.event: A structural, not dated, driver: Kevin Warsh used his first Jackson Hole speech on 2026-08-28 to refuse forward guidance and refuse to publish a reaction function at all, as a stated governance philosophy rather than a one-off. Forward guidance existed to compress the dispersion of expectations about the policy path. Removing it does the opposite by construction, and interest-rate uncertainty is the raw input to CME's largest business.
catalyst.action: Accumulate in halves at 278 and 254 over the next one to two quarters. There is no urgency and no print to front-run. Add on any broad-market drawdown that takes it under 254. The Oct 5 launch of AI compute futures and the Sep 11 start of 24/7 silver are free options, not reasons to hurry.

recommendations.thesis: The Fed just made its own policy path less predictable on purpose, and CME Group is the toll booth on the hedging that creates. The volume response is already visible and it is not subtle: March 2026 ADV was an all-time record 41.1M contracts, +33% year over year, with interest-rate products alone +42% to 20.8M; Q1 set records in both SOFR futures and options (7.5M ADV) and US Treasury futures and options (10.6M ADV); July then set the highest-ever monthly ADV at 27M, +23% year over year. That flows through a business earning $4.27B of net income on $6.76B of revenue — a 63% net margin — because incremental contracts cost the exchange almost nothing to clear.
recommendations.key_risk: Revenue grew only 5.0% over the trailing twelve months while ADV grew 22-33%, which means realised rate per contract is compressing as volume mixes toward cheaper products. If that compression is structural rather than a mix artifact, record volumes stop translating into record revenue and the whole mechanism breaks. The other risk is duller: at 24x trailing and 23x forward this is not a cheap stock, so a multiple de-rating can offset several years of volume growth.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is that this is already priced — CME is 30.9% above its 150-day low and sits above both its 20-day and 50-day averages, and the volume records are public information that the sell side has had since April. The response is the entry discipline rather than a denial: the idea is only taken at 278 and below, which is where the arithmetic works, and the driver is a change in the Fed's operating doctrine that dates from Friday, not from April. RED TEAM — bear case flattered, conviction and size cut. The $240 bear case sits 9.9% ABOVE CME's actual 150-day low of 218.31, a price the stock really traded at this year. Substitute the observed low and the 278 entry returns 1.71, not 2.68 — below the 2.5 floor. The mitigant, and the reason this survives at all, is that the published two-rung plan (278 and 254) averages 266, against the 264.51 that clears 2.5 against the observed low. So the idea works if and only if BOTH rungs actually fill. A single fill at 278 is not this trade. Conviction 4->3 and size 4%->3% accordingly.

recommendations.thesis: The trailing multiple on Medtronic is lying and the reason is documented. MDT shows a 24.46 P/E on $3.73 of TTM EPS against a 15.34 forward P/E, because fiscal 2026 earnings absorbed one-off MiniMed separation costs — roughly 4 cents of IPO dilution plus an 8-cent hit from a one-time $157M charge owed to Blackstone for funding the MiniMed Flex pump — which management stated explicitly is specific to fiscal 2026 and does not affect 2027. Strip that and you are paying 15.3x forward earnings for a business that just delivered its highest annual revenue growth in ten years, grew TTM revenue 8.4% to $36.36B, guides to 6.75-7.25% organic growth, and pays 3.16%.
recommendations.key_risk: Medtronic has spent the better part of a decade guiding to acceleration and then not delivering it, so the FY27 guide is a promise rather than a result — and the Q1 number is flattered by an extra selling week worth 125-150bp of revenue growth and 600-700bp of EPS growth, which management discloses but which makes the headline look better than the underlying. If organic growth settles back near 4%, this is a 15x stock that deserves 15x.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is that the forward multiple is cheap for a reason and the market has correctly refused to pay up for this management team through several previous acceleration stories. That is why the idea waits for the print and buys 3.5% lower rather than now: the discipline is the answer to the objection, and the bear case is priced at $78, close to the 150-day low of $73.31, rather than at some level that flatters the ratio. Insiders offer no support either — 0 open-market buys against 3 sells totalling $595K. RED TEAM — bear case flattered, conviction and size cut. The $78 bear case sits 6.4% ABOVE the actual 150-day low of 73.31. Against the observed low the 88 entry returns 1.77, not 2.60. As with CME the two-rung plan (88 and 82) averages 85, against the 84.94 that clears 2.5 on the observed low — so the arithmetic survives only on a full two-rung fill, not on the first rung alone. Conviction 4->3, size 4%->3%.

watchlist.note: CUT BY RED TEAM — the idea falsified itself and was published anyway. Its own key_risk and counter_argument state that fed funds futures price a September hike at 56-59% while this contract prices 47%, i.e. the deeper and better-capitalised market is 9-12 points more hawkish. The counter_argument then names the error exactly — 'treating that gap as my edge rather than as my error is the exact reasoning that keeps losing trades open' — and takes the position regardless. That is the falsification step being written down and then ignored, which is the specific failure this phase exists to catch. On the report's own stated fair value (September hike 40-45%, so no-change worth 55-60c) the edge against a 54c ask is 1-6 cents on a binary; on the futures-implied fair value of 41-44c it is 10-13 cents NEGATIVE. A 1% lottery ticket with no demonstrated edge is a donation, and the 2.88 reward-to-risk is an artefact of a 38c stop on an event contract, not an expected value. Verified independently against the live Kalshi book: the September strip is H0 53/54c, H25 (25bp hike) 46/47c, tails 1c — the report's prices and polarity are correct (YES on H0 does resolve to no-change), so this is a judgement kill, not a data error. Also note for the record that the validator's 404 on the Kalshi trades endpoint was transient: the URL returns 200 now.
